exposure: Planned mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean)
cohort: 1418 women with singleton breech deliveries at term at Turku University Hospital, Finland, from 2002 to 2012
finding: Planned vaginal breech delivery resulted in short-lasting delayed recovery after birth compared with planned cesarean section, as evidenced by lower Apgar scores at 5 min and umbilical artery pH values.
mod_finding: Planned vaginal breech delivery resulted in short-lasting delayed recovery after birth compared with planned cesarean section, but fewer puerperal infections.
